info.text: Unit 5 — Giving a shift handover briefing. CEFR B2 · EASA Part-66/145. Listening, reading, use of English and vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What work did the technician finish on the A320 left engine?

generalfeedback.text: The technician says: "I have completed the left engine oil change." Present perfect = done and relevant now.

feedback.text: Correct — the oil change was completed and the leak check was dry.

answer.text: A full replacement of the left engine.

feedback.text: No — only the oil was changed, not the engine.

answer.text: A wash of the engine cowling.

feedback.text: No cowling wash is mentioned in the briefing.
Refuelling is not part of this task.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The A320 has an open defect in the tech log.

generalfeedback.text: The technician says the aircraft has no open defect anywhere and the tech log is completely clean.

feedback.text: Incorrect — the tech log is completely clean.
Correct — there is no open defect on aircraft one.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. At what time did the technician run the leak check? Write the time in 24-hour form with no colon (for example, 0930 → 930).

generalfeedback.text: "I ran the leak check at fifteen hundred" = 15:00, written 1500.

feedback.text: Correct — fifteen hundred is 1500.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. How many days does the MEL category C give to rectify the defect?

generalfeedback.text: "The MEL gives us a category C, so we have ten days to rectify it."

feedback.text: Correct — category C = ten days.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. How many steps of the task card had the technician finished?

generalfeedback.text: "I have finished steps one to four already" — so four steps are done; five and six are outstanding.

feedback.text: Correct — steps one to four were finished.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 again. You must not release an aircraft with an open defect unless…

generalfeedback.text: The announcement says: "Do not release any aircraft to service with an open defect, unless the MEL clearly allows it."

feedback.text: Correct — the MEL is the only authority to fly with the item.

answer.text: the day shift supervisor says it is acceptable.

feedback.text: No — a spoken agreement does not authorise flight.

answer.text: the tech log wallet has been signed.

feedback.text: A signature alone does not clear an open defect.

answer.text: the placard has been removed first.

feedback.text: Removing the placard would not make the aircraft legal.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. The borescope is needed for the weather-radar job.

generalfeedback.text: "No, the borescope is not needed at all, because this radar fault is purely electrical."

feedback.text: Incorrect — the fault is electrical, so no borescope is used.
Correct — the borescope is not needed for an electrical fault.

questiontext.text:
Read this Service Bulletin, then answer.

SB 32-1180. Operators must inspect the nose landing gear pin every 500 flight hours. Replace the pin if wear is more than 0.2 mm. This bulletin is recommended, not mandatory.

How often must the pin be inspected?

generalfeedback.text: The SB sets the interval at every 500 flight hours. Wear over 0.2 mm is the replacement limit, not the inspection interval.

feedback.text: Correct — that is the stated inspection interval.

answer.text: Only when the measured wear is above 0.2 mm.

feedback.text: No — 0.2 mm is the replacement limit, not the interval.
The SB does not link the pin to the daily.

answer.text: Once before the aircraft is sold.

feedback.text: Not stated in the bulletin.

questiontext.text:
Read this MEL excerpt, then answer.

MEL 33-45-01, category C. One landing light may be inoperative for up to 10 days. A placard is required. The item must be fixed within the interval.

The aircraft may fly for up to ten days with this item inoperative.

generalfeedback.text: Category C permits the item to be inoperative for up to 10 days, with a placard fitted.

feedback.text: Correct — up to ten days, with a placard.
Incorrect — category C allows ten days.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order, then answer.

Work Order 8841. Task: rectify right landing light. Status: OPEN. Deferred under MEL. Do not sign off until the light works and the placard is removed.

When can the work order be signed off?

generalfeedback.text: The order stays open until the fault is rectified — the light works — and the placard is removed.

feedback.text: Correct — sign off only once it works and the placard is removed.

answer.text: As soon as the placard is first fitted to the switch.

feedback.text: No — fitting the placard opens the deferral, it does not close it.

answer.text: At the start of the next night shift.

feedback.text: The shift does not decide when a job is done.

answer.text: Once ten days have passed by.

feedback.text: Time passing does not fix the fault.

questiontext.text:
Read this BITE readout, then answer.

BITE readout — Weather radar. FAULT 34-41 TRANSCEIVER INTERMITTENT. ANTENNA: PASS. WIRING: CHECK REQUIRED.

The readout shows that the antenna passed its test.

generalfeedback.text: The readout marks the antenna as PASS; the wiring still needs a check and the transceiver fault is intermittent.

feedback.text: Correct — the antenna line reads PASS.
Incorrect — the antenna is marked PASS.

questiontext.text:
Read this Airworthiness Directive, then answer.

AD 2024-07. Mandatory. Inspect the fuel pump wiring for chafing before next flight. Non-compliance grounds the aircraft.

What happens if the operator does not comply with this AD?

generalfeedback.text: An AD is mandatory. Here, non-compliance grounds the aircraft — it may not fly.

feedback.text: Correct — the AD is mandatory and grounds the aircraft.

answer.text: The inspection can be deferred for ten days.

feedback.text: No — an AD is mandatory, not deferrable like an MEL item.

answer.text: A placard must be fitted instead.

feedback.text: A placard does not satisfy a mandatory AD.

answer.text: The tech log is closed for review.

feedback.text: Not stated, and it would not make the aircraft legal.

questiontext.text: Put the verb in the present perfect: "I ___ the daily inspection, so the aircraft is ready." (finish)

generalfeedback.text: Done and relevant now → present perfect: have finished.

feedback.text: Correct.
Also accepted.

questiontext.text: Put the verb in the past simple: "I ___ the leak check at 15:00." (run)

generalfeedback.text: A clear finished time (at 15:00) → past simple: ran.

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text: Write the missing word: "We have not found the cause ___ ."

generalfeedback.text: yet means "up to now" and goes with the present perfect.

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text: Add the missing word: "I ___ already signed the task card."

generalfeedback.text: "already" needs the present perfect, so the auxiliary have is missing. Latvian and Russian have no present perfect, so speakers often drop it.

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text: Which two-word term means a fault that is flown on the MEL and fixed later?

generalfeedback.text: A deferred defect is authorised on the MEL and rectified within the interval.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which verb goes with "a work order"? You ___ a work order.

generalfeedback.text: The natural collocation is raise a work order (not "make" or "do").

feedback.text: Correct.
Accepted.

questiontext.text: Write one word: the aircraft is fit and approved to fly, so it is ___ .

generalfeedback.text: serviceable = fit and approved to use. Its opposite is unserviceable (u/s).

feedback.text: Correct.

questiontext.text: Match each work-status term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: outstanding = not yet done · deferred defect = flown on the MEL, fixed later · carried over = passed to the next shift · open defect = any unfixed fault.

answer.text: still not done; waiting to be finished
a fault flown on the MEL and fixed later
work passed to the next shift to finish
any fault that is still not fixed

questiontext.text: Match each verb to the noun it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: apply the MEL · fit a placard · raise a work order · run a BITE test. These are the natural partner words.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: rectify = fix a defect properly · troubleshoot = find the cause · sign off = certify a job is complete · placard = warning label for an inoperative item.

answer.text: to find the cause of a fault
to certify that a job is complete
a warning label for an inoperative item

questiontext.text: Match each abbreviation to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: MEL = the list of what may be inoperative · AMM = the approved maintenance manual · BITE = the built-in self-test · u/s = unserviceable.

answer.text: the list of what may be inoperative
